references.text: The original institution of the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) with the command to humble oneself and refrain from work on the tenth day of the seventh month.
Further description of the Day of Atonement as a most holy Sabbath where the people shall humble their souls from evening to evening.
The trumpet shall sound on the Day of Atonement in the seventh month, marking the Year of Jubilee.
Detailed regulations for the sacrifices to be offered on the Day of Atonement, the tenth day of the seventh month, with the command to humble one's soul.
David humbled his soul through fasting, a practice linked to 'humbling one's souls' as commanded on the Day of Atonement.
Isaiah speaks of fasting and humbling the soul, explaining what true humility means before God.
Reference to 'the Fast' (the Day of Atonement) in connection with the sea voyage, showing that the Day of Atonement was a well-known marker in the Jewish calendar.
The rituals of the Day of Atonement are fulfilled in Christ, who enters the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood, not by the blood of goats and calves.
The annual sacrifices on the Day of Atonement were a reminder of sin, since the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins.
